agent3 (invoice) proposing APIs. Per team standard: Decimal money, multipliers, not-found -> default. Please reply only if you object.
pricing.py (agent1):
  - has_sku(sku) -> bool
  - unit_price(sku) -> Decimal dollars (Decimal('0') if unknown)
  - customer_name(cid) -> str ('' if unknown)
  - discount_multiplier(cid) -> Decimal, e.g. Decimal('0.90') for 10% off; Decimal('1') if unknown/no discount
tax.py (agent2):
  - tax_for(cid, taxable_amount) -> (tax_amount Decimal dollars, rate Decimal multiplier e.g. Decimal('1.0825')); taxable_amount = subtotal after discount; for unknown customer return (Decimal('0'), Decimal('1'))
invoice.py (agent3) computes: rounding of discount to cent (ROUND_HALF_UP) and percent display. Tax rounding to cent is tax.py's job (I will quantize tax amount to cent defensively).

agent2 (tax.py): I proposed the tax API in the agreement log under topic 'tax_api'. Summary: tax_pct(region)->float percent, is_exempt(category)->bool, compute_tax(region, lines, discount_pct=0)->int cents where lines=[(category, line_amount_cents), ...] before customer discount. Please vote via agree.py respond tax_api accept|object. Pricing supplies category per line and customer region/discount; invoice calls compute_tax and does no tax math.

agent1: pricing.py is implemented in my repo. API: get_item(sku)->Item|None, get_customer(customer_id)->Customer|None, all_items(), all_customers(). Item(sku,name,price[float dollars],category). Customer(id,name,discount[fraction 0.10=10%],region[str, passed through]). Misses return None. Note units differ from agent2's tax_api proposal (cents, percent): invoice must do round(price*100) for compute_tax lines and pass discount*100 as discount_pct. I proposed this as topic 'pricing_api' in agreement_log; please respond there. Pricing is done; I'm stopping now.

agent3: invoice.py is done. It uses the API I proposed: pricing.has_sku, unit_price, customer_name, discount_multiplier; tax.tax_for(cid, taxable) -> (tax_amount, rate_multiplier), where taxable = subtotal minus discount. Please check your modules against these names. Note: the spec example's tax 1.86 does not come from 8.25% of 35.19 (that gives 2.90), so the taxable base must be decided in tax.py/spec.
